run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: OpenTelemetry Demo Astronomy Shop
Namespace: astronomy-shop

An online shopping platform built with a microservices architecture, showcasing OpenTelemetry instrumentation for distributed tracing across services.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: The recommendation path of the Astronomy Shop is broken: the frontend cannot open a TCP connection to the recommendation Service (ClusterIP 10.96.169.211:8080). Every recommendation request from the frontend pod fails with gRPC status 14 UNAVAILABLE and a tcp.connect span error 'connect ETIMEDOUT 10.96.169.211:8080' after up to ~134 s, so the frontend API route returns HTTP 500 and frontend-proxy/load-generator see HTTP 504 after exactly 15 s (mean span duration of frontend 'GET /api/recommendations' 13,947 ms over the last hour). The failure is specific to recommendation: in the same seconds the same frontend pod completed CartService/GetCart and /api/checkout with 200s in 2–40 ms, including a cart pod on sregym-worker, the same node as the recommendation pod. The recommendation pod itself is not crashed: recommendation-78795cd8c-nrm4m is Running and Ready since 13:54:29 with restartCount 0, logged 'Recommendation service started, listening on port 8080' at 13:54:31, its Deployment reports 1/1 available, its Endpoints point at its own pod IP 10.244.234.183:8080, and Calico on sregym-worker programmed that endpoint and reported it up. The object-level anomaly behind this is that the recommendation Service alone (of all application Services in the namespace) has internalTrafficPolicy: Local, while the only recommendation pod runs on sregym-worker and its only client (frontend-6765c5b7c8-r8lks) runs on sregym-worker2 — after the recommendation Deployment was rolled out at 13:53:49/13:54:28 and the frontend pod was rolled onto sregym-worker2 at 13:54:23, the client's node has no local recommendation endpoint, and packets to the ClusterIP are silently dropped (symptom is a connect timeout, not a refusal; the recommendation pod served its last request at 13:54:13 and none afterwards). Traffic counters and spans are consistent with the recommendation application never receiving those SYNs. No crash, OOMKill, eviction, failed probe, Service selector error or enabled flagd fault flag supports an application-level cause.

claims.text: The frontend pod frontend-6765c5b7c8-r8lks fails its recommendation call: span oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations (service frontend) has rpc.grpc.status_code=14 and its child tcp.connect carries otel.status_description 'connect ETIMEDOUT 10.96.169.211:8080', while its dns.lookup children succeed in ~1–38 ms; the enclosing 'GET /api/recommendations' span returned HTTP 500 after 134,480,076 µs.

The recommendation request fails at the edge as well: frontend-proxy 'GET' spans for the same requests error with http.status_code 504 at ~15.0 s (15,001,379 µs) and the matching load-generator 'GET' spans error 504 (15,003,811 µs), while 'router frontend egress' spans last ~15.0 s with http.status_code 0.

Mean span duration over 12:56:18–13:56:18 was 13,947.49 ms for frontend 'GET /api/recommendations' and 13,915.66 ms for load-generator 'user_get_recommendations', versus 51.19–58.37 ms for the frontend's other operations (POST /api/checkout, POST /api/product-ask-ai-assistant/[productId]/index, POST).

The same frontend pod's other calls succeeded while recommendation failed: at 13:56:10–13:56:13 it completed oteldemo.CartService/GetCart with rpc.grpc.status_code=0 in 1.9–3.8 ms and POST /api/checkout with HTTP 200 in ~40 ms, and the cart pod (10.244.234.143) runs on sregym-worker, the same node as the recommendation pod — cross-node traffic from the frontend to sregym-worker was working.

Service recommendation in namespace astronomy-shop (clusterIP 10.96.169.211, selector opentelemetry.io/name=recommendation, port 8080 -> targetPort 8080) is configured with internalTrafficPolicy: Local, whereas Services cart and frontend use internalTrafficPolicy: Cluster.

Of the 27 Services in astronomy-shop, only recommendation and the otel-collector agent Service have internalTrafficPolicy: Local; every other application Service (ad, cart, checkout, currency, email, flagd, frontend, frontend-proxy, kafka, llm, opensearch, payment, postgresql, product-catalog, product-reviews, quote, shipping, valkey-cart) is Cluster.

Node placement makes the Local policy unsatisfiable for this client: the only recommendation pod recommendation-78795cd8c-nrm4m (IP 10.244.234.183) runs on sregym-worker and the only caller frontend-6765c5b7c8-r8lks (IP 10.244.7.215) runs on sregym-worker2; no recommendation pod exists on sregym-worker2.

The recommendation pod is not crashed: recommendation-78795cd8c-nrm4m is Running with Ready=True since 13:54:29, restartCount 0, no lastState termination, no readiness/liveness probe defined, and its own log at 13:54:31 says 'Recommendation service started, listening on port 8080'; deployment recommendation reports 1 available replica.

The recommendation Endpoints are correct: they contain 10.244.234.183:8080, which is the running recommendation pod's own IP and container port; kube_endpoint_address shows the endpoint IP churning 10.244.7.219 (through ~13:54:00) -> 10.244.234.129 (13:54:30–13:55:00) -> 10.244.234.183 (from 13:55:30), matching the two recommendation rollouts in the Deployment events (scale-up of replica set recommendation-6b9dd6f6fc at 13:53:49, scale-up of recommendation-78795cd8c at 13:54:28).

The recommendation Deployment's newest pod template carries annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-21T13:54:28Z, nodeSelector kubernetes.io/hostname=sregym-worker and image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.2.0-recommendation (revision 3); the frontend Deployment is revision 2 with nodeSelector kubernetes.io/hostname=sregym-worker2, and image digests are unchanged across the rolled pods (recommendation sha256:9d3ee28d..., frontend sha256:ead396d0...), i.e. these were configuration-only rollouts.

The recommendation service served its last request at 13:54:13.9: the only recommendation trace returned for 13:54:00–13:56:18 is that end-to-end success (frontend GET /api/recommendations 27,195 µs, recommendation ListRecommendations 4,179 µs, rpc.grpc.status_code=0), and the first failing request from the new frontend pod started at 13:54:28.848, i.e. 5 s after that pod was created at 13:54:23.

No crash-type evidence exists for the recommendation pods: restartCount 0 and no terminated last state, no OOMKilled/Evicted/BackOff events for any recommendation pod, and the only Unhealthy events in astronomy-shop during the window concern grafana, opensearch-0 and otel-collector-agent pods (probe failures while the stack started).

The demo's fault-injection feature flags are not switched on: every flag in ConfigMap flagd-config (including recommendationCacheFailure, productCatalogFailure, cartFailure, paymentFailure, failedReadinessProbe, imageSlowLoad, adFailure) has defaultVariant 'off'.

The CNI did program the current recommendation endpoint: calico-node on sregym-worker logged the workload endpoint 10.244.234.183/32 (interface cali376c96f54b6) with 'status up' at 13:54:28–13:54:29 and removed 10.244.234.129 at 13:55:00, so the pod's veth/endpoint existed on the destination node.

Mechanism: with internalTrafficPolicy: Local and no recommendation endpoint on the client's node (sregym-worker2), the client node's kube-proxy has no destination for the recommendation Service and silently drops the packets, which is why the client sees a TCP connect timeout (SYN unanswered, 127–134 s) instead of a connection refusal, and why the recommendation pod — healthy and listening on 8080 — never logs or serves the request.

The two rapid recommendation rollouts (13:53:49 and 13:54:28) churned the Service endpoint and may have contributed to the earliest failed connections that were mapped to the then-current/deleted pods (10.244.7.219, 10.244.234.129), but endpoint churn alone cannot explain the continued connect timeouts toward the current endpoint 10.244.234.183, which was healthy and programmed from 13:54:29.

Rejected: a node-level network fault on sregym-worker (where the recommendation pod runs). The frontend pod on sregym-worker2 reached the cart pod 10.244.234.143 on that same node repeatedly with rpc.grpc.status_code=0 in 1.9–3.8 ms at 13:56:10–13:56:13, and also reached product-catalog and checkout normally.

Rejected: a Service selector/port or endpoint misconfiguration on recommendation. The Endpoints object holds the running pod's own address 10.244.234.183:8080, the pod carries the selector label opentelemetry.io/name=recommendation, and the Service port/targetPort are 8080 — the same value the application reports listening on.

Restore Service recommendation's internalTrafficPolicy to Cluster (or remove the field) so traffic from the frontend on sregym-worker2 can be routed to the only recommendation endpoint on sregym-worker; the current Local setting can only work if a recommendation pod exists on every client node.

gaps: The exact moment internalTrafficPolicy was set to Local on Service recommendation is unknown: change history is not an integrated source in this Run and Services have no events for spec patches (the object was created at 13:52:51).

kube-proxy logs returned no lines for the window (kube-proxy-cmjb2 on sregym-worker and the worker2 instance), so the silent-drop behaviour itself was not directly observed; it is inferred from the connect-timeout symptom plus the Local policy and node layout.

The query for kind networkpolicies (networking.k8s.io/v1, all namespaces) returned no objects (status no_data), which only shows that no such object matched; Calico CRD policies (projectcalico.org/v3 NetworkPolicy/GlobalNetworkPolicy) and AdminNetworkPolicy objects are not readable with the available tools, so a policy-based drop cannot be excluded from this Run.

The earlier frontend pod (frontend-6859c775df-85pm7) and the earlier recommendation pods (recommendation-5bb649dccb-2ffst, recommendation-6b9dd6f6fc-2ldmd) were deleted before they could be read, so their nodes and logs are unknown and the co-location that made the Local policy work before 13:54:23 is not directly observed.

No baseline before ~13:52 exists (Jaeger's oldest trace for recommendation is 13:54:13 and the stack restarted at 13:52), and the authorized window ends at 13:56:18, so whether the failure persisted or the endpoint/policy changed after 13:56:18 is unknown.
Whether all recommendation traffic is dropped or only the frontend's is unknown; frontend is the only caller of recommendation, so no second client could be checked.
next_steps: Review and, if intended, revert the recommendation Service manifest change that set internalTrafficPolicy: Local (compare with the Helm chart-rendered Service, which uses Cluster for the other application Services).

From a pod on sregym-worker2 verify the drop directly (e.g. a TCP connect to 10.96.169.211:8080 and to 10.244.234.183:8080) and inspect the kube-proxy/iptables KUBE-SVC rule for 10.96.169.211 on that node.

Read the Calico/AdminNetworkPolicy objects (projectcalico.org/v3 NetworkPolicy, GlobalNetworkPolicy, policy.networking.k8s.io AdminNetworkPolicy) to rule out any additional packet drop selecting recommendation pods.

Consider whether the Deployment node pins (recommendation -> sregym-worker, frontend -> sregym-worker2) are intentional; with internalTrafficPolicy Cluster they are harmless, with Local they guarantee this outage.
